steps: Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A) came with the 42nd Amendment, 1976, during the Emergency.
The committee whose report shaped the 42nd Amendment was the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee (1976).
Justice Varma (Verma) Committee of 1999 only studied how to operationalise the duties - it did not add them; Kripalani and Ram Nandan are unrelated.
-> answer (a) Swaran Singh Committee
fact: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the Fundamental Duties, added as Article 51A by the 42nd Amendment.

steps: The Preamble has been amended only once - by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 (the 'mini-Constitution').
It inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'; the 44th Amendment (1978) undid Emergency excesses but did not touch these words.
-> answer (b) 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
fact: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

steps: Surest pair: Concurrent List comes from Australia -> c-ii. This strikes (a) (c-v) and (d) (c-i).
Left (b) and (c): Emergency provisions come from the Government of India Act, 1935 (a-iii), not the USA (a-v) -> strike (b).
Check (c): suspension of FRs in emergency from the Weimar (German) Constitution b-iv, single citizenship from UK d-i - consistent.
-> answer (c) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
fact: Concurrent List from Australia, Emergency provisions from GoI Act 1935, suspension of FRs from Germany, single citizenship from the UK.

steps: Surest: the 97th Amendment added Part IX-B (co-operative societies), not Part X-B (Part IX-A is municipalities) -> C is false.
Strike (b) and (d), which include C.
Between (a) A, B, D and (c) A, B: the same Amendment inserted Article 43B (DPSP to promote co-operatives) -> D is true.
-> answer (a) A, B and D only

underline.why: wrong part number: it is IX-B

fact: The 97th Amendment (2011) added 'co-operative societies' to Art. 19(1)(c), Article 43B and Part IX-B.

steps: Ambedkar called the right to constitutional remedies the 'heart and soul' - without a remedy, every other right is empty.
Right to constitutional remedies = Article 32 (writs to the Supreme Court). Art. 14 is equality, 25/26 are religion.
-> answer (b) Article 32
fact: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) the heart and soul of the Constitution.

steps: Two dates to keep apart: adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day), came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
The question says 'adopted' -> November 1949. Strike January 1949 (Assembly still debating) and November 1950 (after the Constitution was already in force).
-> answer (c) November 26th, 1949

underline.why: trap: date it came into force

fact: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950.

steps: Recall the sequence: Part III FRs, Part IV DPSP, Part IV-A Duties, Part V The Union, Part VI The States.
Union Executive (President, VP, Council of Ministers, Arts. 52-78) sits in Part V. Part VII was repealed in 1956.
-> answer (d) Part V
fact: Part V (Articles 52-151) deals with the Union, including the Union Executive.

steps: Count back from 12 Schedules: 12th and 11th added in 1992 (74th/73rd), 10th in 1985 (52nd), 9th in 1951 (1st Amendment).
So the original Constitution had 12 - 4 = 8 Schedules; 9 and 10 are later additions, 7 is the Seventh Schedule trap.
-> answer (a) 8
fact: The original Constitution had 8 Schedules; the 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th were added later.

steps: Link it to the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 - the Act and the NHRC share the year.
NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 (first by ordinance), the year of the Vienna World Conference on Human Rights.
-> answer (c) 1993
fact: The National Human Rights Commission was constituted on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

steps: Minorities - Justice Mohammad Sardar Ali Khan (b-iii) is in every code, so it does not help.
Next surest: the first NCST (2004) chairperson was Kunwar Singh (Tekam) -> a-ii. Strike (a) a-iv and (c) a-i.
Left (b) and (d): the NCBC of 1993 (set up after the Mandal judgment) was headed by a judge, Justice R. N. Prasad -> d-i; Suraj Bhan headed the NCSC -> c-iv.
-> answer (d) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
fact: First chairpersons: NCST Kunwar Singh, NCM Justice M. Sardar Ali Khan, NCSC Suraj Bhan, NCBC Justice R. N. Prasad.

steps: A: residuary powers are given to Parliament by Article 248 (plus Entry 97, Union List) -> true.
B is just the definition of residuary power - matters in no List belong exclusively to Parliament. 'exclusive' looks extreme but is exactly what Art. 248 says -> true.
-> answer (c) Both A and B
fact: Article 248 vests residuary legislative power exclusively in Parliament.

steps: Surest pair: Habeas Corpus = 'to have the body of' -> c-iv. Strike (c) c-ii and (d) c-iii.
Left (a) and (b): Mandamus = 'we command' -> b-iii. Strike (a) b-i.
Check (b): Quo warranto 'by what authority' a-ii, Certiorari 'to be certified' d-i.
-> answer (b) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
fact: Quo warranto: by what authority; Mandamus: we command; Habeas corpus: to have the body; Certiorari: to be certified.

steps: Judicial review began with Marbury v. Madison (1803) in the US Supreme Court; the term 'judicial activism' was coined in the USA (1947).
Strike UK (parliamentary sovereignty, no judicial review of statutes) and USSR (no independent judiciary); India adopted it later.
-> answer (a) USA
fact: Judicial activism and judicial review originated in the USA (Marbury v. Madison, 1803).

steps: The State Election Commission was created by the 73rd/74th Amendments - Art. 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities).
State Legislature elections are run by the Election Commission of India (Art. 324); co-operative elections go to separate co-operative authorities.
-> answer (a) Local Bodies
fact: The State Election Commission conducts panchayat and municipal elections (Arts. 243K, 243ZA).

steps: Earliest: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) -> d first. Strike (b), which starts with b.
Latest: Gadgil Committee (1988), after L. M. Singhvi (1986) -> sequence must end with a. Strike (a) and (c), which end with c.
Check (d): Dantwala 1978 sits between 1957 and 1986.
-> answer (d) d, b, c, a
fact: Balwant Rai Mehta 1957, Dantwala 1978, L. M. Singhvi 1986, Gadgil 1988.

steps: Both Amendments were passed in December 1992, so no 1992 date can be the commencement -> strike (b) and (d).
24 April 1993 is the 73rd Amendment's date (National Panchayati Raj Day) - a pair-trap. The 74th followed on 1 June 1993.
-> answer (c) 1st June, 1993
fact: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993 and the 74th on 1 June 1993.

steps: C is the surest: Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution made him the Father of Local Self-Government -> true (in every option).
B: Madras got India's first municipal corporation in 1688 -> true. Strike (a) and (d), which leave out B.
A: the Cantonments Act was passed by the Central Legislature in 1924 -> true, so (c) is out.
-> answer (b) A, B and C
fact: India's first municipal corporation was set up at Madras in 1688; Lord Ripon (1882) is the Father of Local Self-Government.

steps: Mind the stem: it asks which is NOT true.
A: Goa's 1999 Assembly election was the first held with EVMs statewide -> true, so A is not the answer; strike (a) and (b).
B: the 1998 trial covered 16 seats in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi - Gujarat is a swapped name -> B is not true.
-> answer (c) Only B
fact: EVMs were first tried in 1998 in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi, and used statewide first in Goa in 1999.

steps: Voting age 21 -> 18 changed Article 326 through the 61st Amendment, 1988 (Rajiv Gandhi era), effective 1989.
73rd is panchayats - strike it; 60th (profession tax) and 69th (Delhi NCT) are unrelated.
-> answer (a) 61st Amendment Act
fact: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 (Art. 326).

steps: Surest pair: Vohra Committee (1993, after the Bombay blasts) studied the nexus between crime and politics -> a-v.
Only (d) has a-v -> strike (a), (b), (c).
Check (d): Indrajit Gupta - state funding (b-iii), Dinesh Goswami - electoral reforms (c-iv), J. S. Verma - criminal law amendments after 2012 (d-i).
-> answer (d) a-v, b-iii, c-iv, d-i

underline.text: v. Nexus between crime and politics

fact: Vohra: crime-politics nexus; Indrajit Gupta: state funding of elections; Dinesh Goswami: electoral reforms; J. S. Verma: criminal law.

steps: Check the appointing body in B: the CEC is appointed by the President, not by the Chief Justice -> B is false.
Strike (a), (c), (d) - all contain B.
Confirm (b): ECI is constitutional (Art. 324) and has been a three-member body since 1993.
-> answer (b) A and C

underline.text: appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India

fact: The Election Commission is a constitutional body (Art. 324) whose CEC and ECs are appointed by the President.

steps: Ask of each body: is it created by an Article of the Constitution?
NITI Aayog - executive resolution (2015); NCM - National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992; NHRC - Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993: none constitutional.
Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities - Article 350B (7th Amendment, 1956) -> constitutional. Count = 1.
-> answer (b) 1
fact: Of these, only the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art. 350B) is a constitutional body.

steps: The 91st Amendment (2003) inserted Art. 75(1A): the Union Council of Ministers, PM included, may not exceed 15% of Lok Sabha strength.
12 is a trap - it is the minimum number of ministers in a State under Art. 164(1A), not a percentage.
-> answer (d) 15 percent
fact: The 91st Amendment caps the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(1A)).

steps: Pair the phrases with authors: Ivor Jennings - 'federation with a strong centralising tendency'; K. C. Wheare - 'quasi-federal'.
Nehru and H. V. Kamath are not the authors of either label.
-> answer (a) Ivor Jennings

underline.text: a federation with a centralising tendency

fact: Ivor Jennings called India a federation with a strong centralising tendency; K. C. Wheare called it quasi-federal.

steps: Article 124(1) fixes the Supreme Court strength 'until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number'.
So Parliament increases it (e.g. the 2019 Act raised it to 34). The collegium only recommends names; the President appoints but cannot add posts; Law Commission only advises.
-> answer (c) Parliament
fact: Parliament can increase the number of Supreme Court judges by law (Art. 124(1)).

steps: Earliest: DMK (1949) -> B first. Strike (b), which starts with D.
Latest: Samajwadi Party (1992), founded after the BSP (1984) -> sequence must end with A. Strike (c) and (d), which end with C.
Check (a): TDP 1982 comes after DMK and before BSP 1984.
-> answer (a) B, D, C, A
fact: DMK 1949, TDP 1982, BSP 1984, Samajwadi Party 1992.

steps: RTI selection committees are political-executive: CM (or PM), Leader of Opposition and a minister - no judge sits on them.
So B (Chief Justice of the High Court) is the odd member -> strike (a), (c), (d), which contain B.
-> answer (b) A, C and D

underline.text: Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court

fact: Under Sec. 15(3) of the RTI Act, the State CIC is chosen by the CM, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM.

steps: Surest: Governor (Centre's appointee) and Emergency powers are classic unitary features -> A and D in; every option has A.
B says 'Central Services' - these serve only the Union, unlike All India Services, so they do not touch State autonomy -> B out; strike (a).
C: one CAG audits both Union and State accounts - a unitary feature -> C in; strike (c) and (d).
-> answer (b) A, C and D
fact: Office of Governor, a single CAG and Emergency powers are unitary features that depart from federal principles.

steps: Surest pair: Education moved to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 -> c-i. Strike (c) and (d).
Left (a) and (b): organisation of High Courts is Union List entry 78 -> a-ii. Strike (b).
Check (a): taxes on mineral rights is State List entry 50 -> b-iii.
-> answer (a) a-ii, b-iii, c-i
fact: Organisation of High Courts: Union List; taxes on mineral rights: State List; education: Concurrent List (since 1976).

steps: Climb the title ladder: Regulating Act 1773 - Governor-General of Bengal; Charter Act 1833 - Governor-General of India; GoI Act 1858 - Viceroy.
So 'Bengal -> India' is the 1833 step (Lord William Bentinck). 1793 and 1853 only renewed the Charter.
-> answer (c) Charter Act of 1833
fact: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Bentinck).

steps: Timeline: Parliament passed it in December 2013 (17-18 Dec), the President gave assent on 1 January 2014.
It came into force later, on 16 January 2014. 1 January is the assent trap; December dates are before assent.
-> answer (b) 16th January 2014
fact: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 got assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014.

steps: Surest false: D. The Art. 249 resolution in the national interest belongs only to the Rajya Sabha (the House of the States), not the Lok Sabha.
Strike (a) and (b), which contain D.
B is the correct Art. 249 Rajya Sabha resolution -> true, so (d) A and C is too short.
-> answer (c) A, B and C only

underline.text: The Lok Sabha passes a resolution
The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution

fact: Parliament may legislate on State subjects under Art. 249 (Rajya Sabha resolution), 250 (emergency), 252 (two or more States' request) and 253 (international agreements).

steps: The 11th duty, Art. 51A(k) (parents to educate children aged 6-14), came with the RTE package that also added Art. 21A.
That is the 86th Amendment, enacted in 2002 - strike the 96th (2011, 'Odia' spelling) and the wrong year 2001.
-> answer (b) 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002
fact: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty (Art. 51A(k)) together with Art. 21A.

steps: A: UPSC recruits for the Union services -> true.
R: UPSC is an independent constitutional body (Art. 315) -> true.
Does R explain A? Its status does not make it the recruiting agency - its functions under Art. 320 do -> not the explanation.
-> answer (b) Both true, R is not a correct explanation
fact: The UPSC is the central recruiting agency and an independent constitutional body under Article 315.

steps: A: the 73rd Amendment is the landmark of grassroots democracy -> true.
R: it moved panchayats from Art. 40 (non-justiciable DPSP) into Part IX, the justiciable Constitution -> true.
Constitutional status is precisely why it is a landmark -> R explains A.
-> answer (a) Both true, R is the correct explanation

underline.why: the reason it is a landmark

fact: The 73rd Amendment gave panchayats constitutional status by placing them in Part IX.

steps: A: 'violate' sounds strong, but the known criticism is that All India Services dilute federalism and State autonomy -> true.
R: AIS officers serve States but are governed by central rules; States cannot fully control them -> true.
R names the exact mechanism behind A's criticism -> R explains A.
-> answer (a) Both true, R is the correct explanation
fact: All India Service officers are controlled by central rules, which is why they are said to dilute State autonomy.

steps: A: NITI Aayog was set up by an executive resolution (1 January 2015) -> non-constitutional advisory body, true.
R: village-level planning aggregated upward is one of its stated objectives -> true.
A is about legal status, R about an objective - different topics -> R does not explain A.
-> answer (b) Both true, R is not the correct explanation
fact: NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional, non-statutory body created by executive resolution in 2015.

steps: A: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council -> true.
R: the Rajamannar Committee (1969) did press for setting it up -> true.
A 1969 report cannot explain a provision that existed since 1950 -> R does not explain A.
-> answer (b) Both true, R is not a correct explanation
fact: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council; it was actually set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.

steps: Surest false: C says 'all' Fundamental Rights - since the 44th Amendment Arts. 20 and 21 can never be suspended.
Strike (b) and (d), which contain C.
B: under Art. 353 the Centre can direct a State on any matter during a national emergency -> true, so (c) 'Only A' is too short.
-> answer (a) A and B only

underline.text: executive directions to a State on any matter

fact: During a national emergency Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment).

steps: Surest false: B. PIL is the product of judicial activism, the opposite of judicial restraint.
Strike (b), (c), (d), which contain B.
-> answer (a) A and C only
fact: PIL (social action litigation) grew out of judicial activism, pioneered by Justices Krishna Iyer and P. N. Bhagwati.

steps: Sarkaria (1983), Rajamannar (1969) and Punchhi (2007) are all Centre-State relations reviews.
Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) was on state funding of elections -> the odd one.
-> answer (b) Indrajit Guptha Committee
fact: Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections; Sarkaria, Rajamannar and Punchhi dealt with Centre-State relations.

steps: National party status (Election Symbols Order, para 6B) needs any one of three alternatives.
(a) 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least 3 States, (b) 6% votes in 4 States plus 4 Lok Sabha seats, (c) State party in 4 States - all three are real conditions.
None of them is 'not a condition', so 'None of the above' stands.
-> answer (d) None of the above
fact: A party is a National Party if it meets any one of: 2% LS seats from 3 States; 6% votes in 4 States + 4 LS seats; State party in 4 States.

steps: Stem asks 'not correct'. A: the Eleventh Schedule has 29 items; 18 is the Twelfth Schedule count -> A not correct (in every option).
D: BC reservation is left to the States (voluntary) -> D not correct; strike (c), which lacks D.
B is correct (Art. 243M excludes Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram) -> strike (b); C is correct (Art. 243O bars courts) -> strike (d).
-> answer (a) A and D only
fact: The 73rd Amendment lists 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule and leaves BC reservation to the States.

steps: Surest: nominated members do not vote in the Presidential election (they do vote for the Vice-President) -> B and D out.
Strike (a) and (b), which contain B and D.
E: the 70th Amendment (1992) added elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry -> true, so (d) A and C is short.
-> answer (c) A, C and E
fact: The President's electoral college has only elected MPs and elected MLAs of States, Delhi and Puducherry (Art. 54).

steps: 2015 + struck down = NJAC, the Fourth Judges case (16 October 2015).
NJAC was created by the 99th Amendment, 2014. The 100th (2015) was the India-Bangladesh land boundary; 97th co-operatives; 96th 'Odia'.
-> answer (d) 99th Constitutional Amendment Act
fact: The Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment (NJAC) in October 2015.

steps: Surest: separate electorates for Muslims came with the Morley-Minto Act, 1909 -> a-iii. Strike (c) a-iv.
Proposed All-India Federation = GoI Act, 1935 -> c-i. Strike (d) c-ii. Dyarchy 1919 (b-v) is common to all.
Left (a) and (b): discussion of the annual financial statement was first allowed by the 1892 Act -> d-ii. Strike (b) d-iv.
-> answer (a) a-iii, b-v, c-i, d-ii

underline.text: a. Separate representation of the Muslim Community

fact: 1861: councils; 1892: budget discussion; 1909: separate electorates; 1919: dyarchy; 1935: federation.

steps: Stem asks the incorrect statement.
Quasi-judicial, Chairman plus four members and advisory role are all true features of the Finance Commission.
Its Article is 280, not 290 (Art. 290 is about expenses and pensions) -> (d) is incorrect.
-> answer (d) Article 290 provides for the Constitution of Finance Commission
fact: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280.

steps: Recall the Preamble: 'LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship'.
Options (b), (c), (d) all match the 'Liberty of ...' list. 'Political' belongs to JUSTICE (social, economic and political), not liberty.
-> answer (a) Political Liberty
fact: The Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and justice - social, economic and political.

steps: Surest false: iii. The AG holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 76(4)), not the Prime Minister. Strike (c) and (d).
iv is also false: remuneration is fixed by the President, not Parliament.
ii: right of audience in all courts in India (Art. 76(3)) -> true, so (b) 'Only i' is too short.
-> answer (a) Only i and ii
fact: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has right of audience in all courts in India.

steps: Surest pair: Directive Principles come from the Irish Constitution -> b-iii.
Only (b) has b-iii -> strike (a), (c), (d).
Check (b): UK rule of law (a-ii), USA judicial review (c-iv), Canada residuary powers with Centre (d-i).
-> answer (b) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i

underline.text: iii. Directive Principles of State Policy

fact: Borrowed: Rule of law (UK), DPSP (Ireland), judicial review (USA), residuary powers with the Centre (Canada).

steps: Surest false: iv. Accountability to the legislature is the parliamentary feature; a President has a fixed term and is not accountable to Congress.
Strike (a) and (d), which contain iv.
ii: the US President is head of State and head of Government -> true, so (b) i and iii is short.
-> answer (c) Only i, ii and iii are correct
fact: In a presidential system the President is both head of state and of government, directly elected and not accountable to the legislature.

steps: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243-I for panchayats, 243Y for municipalities) is set up every 5 years to review local finances -> i true.
Its recommendations cover State-local sharing of taxes and, since it covers both panchayats and municipalities, rural-urban sharing too -> ii true.
-> answer (c) Both i and ii

underline.text: financial position of the local governments
between rural and urban local governments

fact: The State Finance Commission (Arts. 243-I, 243Y) reviews the finances of panchayats and municipalities and recommends revenue sharing.

steps: i (five-year term, Art. 67) and ii (ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Art. 64) are sure -> strike (b) and (c).
iii has the trap word 'only', but here it holds: under Art. 65 the VP acts only until a new President is elected and enters office.
-> answer (d) All i, ii and iii

underline.text: only until a new President is elected
ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

fact: The Vice President has a five-year term, chairs the Rajya Sabha and acts as President only until a new President is elected.

steps: 'Free to raise any matter' = no prior notice needed. Question Hour (first hour) allows only admitted questions with notice.
Zero Hour (from 12 noon) is the informal Indian innovation for raising urgent matters without notice -> strike Question Hour and 'Both'.
-> answer (a) Zero hour
fact: Zero Hour is an informal Indian practice for raising urgent matters without prior notice.

steps: The strongest weapon is the one that can remove the government: under Art. 75(3) the ministry must resign if a no-confidence motion passes in the Lok Sabha.
Question Hour and Zero Hour only seek answers; elections are not a parliamentary device.
-> answer (a) No Confidence Motion
fact: A no-confidence motion, which can remove the Council of Ministers, is Parliament's strongest tool for executive accountability.

steps: Surest: Art. 32 = Supreme Court writs for Fundamental Rights -> d-i. Strike (c) d-ii and (d) d-iii.
Art. 226 = High Court writs -> b-iii. (a) has b-iv, so strike it.
Check (b): Art. 137 SC review power (a-ii), Art. 13 laws void if inconsistent (c-iv).
-> answer (b) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
fact: Art. 137: SC review; Art. 226: HC writs; Art. 13: void laws; Art. 32: SC writs for FRs.

steps: Art. 370 was effectively removed in August 2019, and the Reorganisation Act was passed the same month - it is the 2019 Act.
An Act passed in 2019 cannot take effect in 2017 or 2018; it took effect on 31 October 2019 (Sardar Patel's birthday) - 2020 is too late.
-> answer (a) 31st October 2019
fact: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 took effect on 31 October 2019, creating the UTs of J&K and Ladakh.

steps: A: property is a constitutional/legal right under Art. 300-A, Part XII -> true.
R: the 44th Amendment (1978) removed property (Arts. 19(1)(f), 31) from the Fundamental Rights -> true.
The same amendment that removed it from Part III placed it in Art. 300-A, so R is the cause of A -> explains.
-> answer (a) Both true, R is the correct explanation
fact: The 44th Amendment (1978) made property a legal right under Article 300-A instead of a Fundamental Right.

steps: Mehta vs Mehta: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) = three tiers; Ashok Mehta (1978) = two tiers (Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat).
Ashok Mehta also proposed a four-year term -> strike all three-tier options and the five-year one.
-> answer (a) two tier system with four years of term

underline.text: two tier system with four years of term

fact: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1978) recommended a two-tier panchayat system with a four-year term.

steps: Under Art. 74 the President makes appointments on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM.
Surest: Governors (iv) are appointed on the PM's advice. Only (d) contains iv -> strike (a), (b), (c).
-> answer (d) All of the above
fact: Formally the President makes high appointments on the advice of the PM-led Council of Ministers (Art. 74).

steps: Surest false: ii. Art. 243E requires elections within six months of dissolution, not three.
Strike (a), (b), (d), which contain ii.
Check (c): direct election, one-third reservation for women and minimum age 21 are all correct.
-> answer (c) i, iii and iv only
fact: Under Art. 243E, panchayat elections must be held within six months of dissolution.

steps: A: Article 356 (President's Rule) is among the most controversial Articles, misused over 100 times -> true.
R: it is imposed when a State's government cannot be carried on as per the Constitution -> true (the text of Art. 356).
That broad, subjective ground is what allowed the misuse -> R explains A (key).
-> answer (a) Both true, R is the correct explanation

underline.text: cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution

fact: Article 356 allows President's Rule when a State's government cannot be carried on as per the Constitution.

steps: A: courts do not issue mandamus ordering the government to make a law (separation of powers) -> true.
R: mandamus enforces an existing duty or policy; it cannot lie where no policy exists -> true.
R states the rule from which A follows -> explains.
-> answer (a) Both true, R is the correct explanation

underline.text: not issued to Govt. for making law
cannot lie in absence of policy

fact: Mandamus enforces existing legal duties or policies; it is not issued to direct the legislature or government to make law.

steps: A: DPSPs are non-justiciable (Art. 37) -> true.
R: they guide legislation and governance -> true.
Being a guide is their role, not the reason they cannot be enforced (Art. 37 says so expressly) -> not the explanation. APPSC's final key confirms (b).
-> answer (b) Both true, R is not the correct explanation

underline.text: not capable of being independently enforced

fact: Article 37 makes the Directive Principles non-justiciable, though fundamental in governance.

steps: Both lines are the wording of Article 39 (DPSP): (b) distribution of ownership of material resources for the common good, (c) no concentration of wealth to the common detriment.
They are the twin socialist clauses; recalling 39(b)/(c) settles both -> both present.
-> answer (b) Both Statements (A) and (B) are present
fact: Article 39(b) and 39(c) direct fair distribution of material resources and prevention of concentration of wealth.

steps: Options are nested; only (d) contains e. So decide e first.
Protection of monuments and places of national importance is Article 49, a DPSP -> e is in. Strike (a), (b), (c).
Confirm: 39A legal aid, 42 maternity relief, 43 living wage, 48A forests are all DPSPs.
-> answer (d) a, b, c, d and e
fact: Free legal aid (39A), maternity relief (42), living wage (43), forests (48A) and monuments (49) are all Directive Principles.

steps: Eleventh Schedule = Panchayats (rural, 29 items); Twelfth = Municipalities (urban, 18 items).
Slaughter houses, regulation of land use (urban planning) and burial grounds are urban civic functions -> Twelfth Schedule.
Libraries is the odd one - item 20 of the Eleventh Schedule.
-> answer (a) Libraries
